Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. historical_references.reference: Tushala Danam is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an Indian epic poem that is part of the Hindu Mahabharata tradition. It is believed to have been written between 400 BCE and 200 CE.
historical_references.context: Tushala Danam is a village that is significant in the Mahabharata as it is here that the Pandava brothers, led by Bhima, are supposed to have stayed for a year incognito after their exile. They are hosted by the local king, Virata, who mistakes them for his army and sends them to fight in a war.

historical_references.reference: Tushala is also mentioned in the Jain text, Harivamsha, as a city ruled by the king Ayushman. The text is believed to have been written between 400 BCE and 200 CE, making it approximately contemporary with the Mahabharata.
historical_references.context: In the Harivamsha, Tushala is described as a prosperous city with beautiful gardens and temples, ruled by King Ayushman. The city is significant in the text as it is here that the Jain saint Bhagavani Mahavira visits during his final days. The city's people are said to have been deeply moved by his teachings and made offerings to him.
